I'll cut out the long boring explanation I just typed and simply say that about thirteen years ago I got to a point where I'd gained about forty extra pounds in a year or so. One day Husband and I got dressed up and went out to dinner; before we left my MIL took a photo of us, and seeing that photo just horrified me. Seeing how my features had become just erased and changed by extra fat, how truly dumpy I looked, how I was only 33 but looked ten years older...that was it, that very moment. The next day I started researching calories counting and how to do it; two days later I did my first 1200 calorie day, and six/seven months later I'd lost 42 pounds and was a size 0/2. It felt amazing. Not just being thin, but the feeling of knowing, truly knowing deep down, that my weight was in MY control, that it was directly related to what I ate, that I could be a size 0 and I could look fantastic in tight dresses and snug jeans--in fact, that I didn't even need to try things on anymore because no matter what it was, it would look good.

I'm currently about five pounds over where I want to be, so I'm back down to 1200/day until it's gone again. I'm not worried or upset about it, because I know how easy it is to lose it, and I know that even five pounds over what I like is still thin, still well in the normal BMI range, and still waaaaay smaller than "the average woman." When I was heavy, gaining five pounds was a tragedy, a horrifying and shameful thing...now it's nbd, because I know exactly how/why it happened (summer heat keeps me from walking as much, being forced to be indoors all day means I bake because I'm bored, eating extra brownies exacerbates the effect of the reduced walks) and how to stop it and reverse it with ease.

It is genuinely true that no food tastes as good as thin feels...and what fats and their "I'm going to enjoy muh food, unlike you skinny thing-privilege bitches," don't realize is that being thin means you truly can enjoy delicious treats without guilt, because they're just a treat you enjoy, not a symbol of your failure, laziness, or gluttony, and not a stupid and self-defeating attempt to Stick It To The Man. Sometimes a brownie is just a brownie.

(Did I mention that I make awesome brownies, lol?)

This is awesome. I'm about to turn 30 and wanted to lose 5 or 10 pounds. Did the same research - calorie counting. Was super easy to get started and get back to the slim I wanted. I wish more people realized it's directly under their control (and that frankly, it's as easy as as low daily calorie counting!).

Lol, I remember being shocked by how simple and easy it was, and thinking I must be doing something wrong because I was still eating whatever I wanted (just in much smaller portions). I'd pretty much always been slim, so the only times I'd read diet books or looked into diets were during and in the aftermath of my first pregnancy--Atkins, the Zone, and some book specifically on losing baby weight--and they'd all been complex. Like, not complicated, just complex (well, Atkins wasn't, but you know what I mean; these were books that kept talking about insulin and hormones and "set points" and two-week-kickstarts with lists of forbidden foods and acceptable snacks for particular times of day and such). So when I started counting calories, and at the end of the day felt totally satisfied but still had two hundred left and was deciding between a piece of cake or a vodka tonic or an entire pack of Starburst or something it was like, this can't really be this easy, can it?

But it was. And then I felt like a moron for not doing it sooner.

And like I said, that was thirteen years ago now and I've basically kept it off; I hover around 105 instead of 100-102 these days, and like I said at the moment I have a couple to lose because I've been lazy, but I certainly have never crossed even 115 again (even a few years ago when I went through a major depressive episode and basically did nothing but sit and mope, overeating and overdrinking), much less 140. My stomach just isn't big enough for all that food anymore, I don't like the way it feels to overeat, I found better ways to fill my time than eating and watching TV... Basically, I'm just too happy being thin.
